text.tspan: Expands: Reservation Rules (03-components). Conceptual TypeScript classes/functions and contracts; no implementation required.
RESERVATION RULES [Component inside Board Web App]
Never trusts a student ID submitted in a form.
AuthContext = VerifiedStudent {studentId: StudentId, name: string, email: Email} | Unauthenticated
Workshop = {id: WorkshopId, ownerId: StudentId, title: string, start: Timestamp, capacity: integer, published: boolean}
Reservation = {id: ReservationId, workshopId: WorkshopId, studentId: StudentId, name: string, email: Email, createdAt: Timestamp}
Not called for Existing or Rejected.
New { reservation: Reservation, email: Requested | Unavailable } - newly committed seat; one confirmation attempt.
Existing { reservation: Reservation, email: NotRequested } - the exact saved record; no update, insert or email.
Rejected { reason: Unauthenticated | WorkshopNotFound | NotPublished | Full } - no reservation change or email.
StorageFailure - persistence/commit could not be confirmed; do not claim success or request email; refresh reads authoritative state.
WorkshopId / StudentId / ReservationId are distinct string types; Timestamp is an instant; Email is an email address.
1. Reject Unauthenticated before any reservation lookup or mutation.
2. Workshop Store begins a READ COMMITTED transaction.
3. SELECT workshop WHERE id = wid FOR UPDATE; missing -> reject.
4. In a separate statement, find this student's existing reservation.
If found, return that record unchanged (even when full).
5. For a new seat, require published; count seats in a later statement.
If count >= capacity, reject Full without writes.
6. Insert one new reservation with the verified student ID/name/email.
COMMIT before returning Created from Workshop Store.
7. Only Created triggers Confirmation.requestOnce; return New.
All reservation writers lock the same workshop row
until commit; no direct write path bypasses Store.
A waiting caller reads existing/count after acquiring
the lock, using new READ COMMITTED statements.
Thus it sees prior commits before deciding to insert.
Workshop.id primary key; foreign key from each seat.
Mail failure cannot undo an already committed seat.
Legend: blue = code elements inside Reservation Rules; grey = supporting component interfaces outside that parent; green/orange = explanation.
Dashed outline = expanded component; arrows = calls or type dependencies. Promise<T> = asynchronous result; Tx = transaction-scoped interface.
